title: Atlas TransitionCase structural contract v1
description: Closed R2.0 structural schema. cisco_toolkit.transition_contract remains authoritative for canonical-byte, ordering, digest, identity, temporal, scope, and replay joins that JSON Schema cannot express.
$comment: Qualification state is deliberately absent from applicability. Qualification authority is derived from independently supplied, digest-bound receipts under the evaluation-time trust policy.

identifierSet.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires lexicographic canonical order.

possiblyEmptyIdentifierSet.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires lexicographic canonical order.

evidenceStatus.$comment: Closed evaluator vocabulary; not a caller-set TransitionCase authority field.

qualificationState.$comment: For independently supplied qualification receipts or pack manifests only; never an applicability input.

authoritativeGate.$comment: Closed evaluator output vocabulary; not a caller-set TransitionCase authority field.

digestSet.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires lexicographic canonical order.

possiblyEmptyDigestSet.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires lexicographic canonical order.

imports.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires lexicographic canonical order.

wasm_modules.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires canonical ordering and uniqueness by module_id.

claim_boundary.const: EXPERIMENTAL draft for contract, fixture, and replay work only; never qualified, GA, authoritative, portable, or promotion-eligible before R2.6

tcbManifestV1.$comment: Migration-read-only v1 manifests cannot freeze budgets or activate packs.

tcbManifestV2.$comment: The Python validator additionally enforces ordering, source/interpreter joins, measured executable-line counts, and externally verified budget-review bindings.

qualificationReceipt.$comment: The Python validator proves issued_at <= valid_from < valid_until. Effective EXPIRED or REVOKED state is derived from independently supplied evaluation-time trust policy.

timeInterval.$comment: The Python validator additionally proves start_inclusive <= end_inclusive.

transitionIdentity.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires distinct before/after digests and exact identity joins.

accepted_evidence_classes.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires canonical order.

obligations.$comment: The Python validator enforces sorted unique obligation IDs, unique requirement IDs, and subject/state scope.

evolutionIr.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires different from/to states, no intermediate collision, and root identity equality.

qualificationDenominator.$comment: The Python validator closes denominator kind by subject kind and observation mode, requires inspectable event/model preimages, and joins observation/applicability identity, predicates, subjects, platform releases, and time windows.

qualificationEvidenceBinding.$comment: The Python validator requires exact coverage of every non-null qualification receipt, canonical receipt ordering, unique signatures, and mandatory replay-content bindings for all three proof objects.

transformStep.$comment: The Python validator additionally requires reminted bytes and transform-chain digest continuity.

canonicalValue.$comment: Floats are forbidden. The Python canonical encoder additionally enforces NFC, UTF-8 byte limits, depth/node guards, unique object keys, and sorted canonical object encoding.

evidenceAtom.$comment: The Python validator proves exact transition identity, subject/state/profile scope, evidence time order, window containment, predicate joins, and transform continuity.

applicability.$comment: There is intentionally no qualification_state property; additionalProperties=false rejects caller-injected authority.

derivation.$comment: The Python validator joins obligation/evidence IDs, scopes, evidence classes, semantic profiles, temporal semantics, and evaluator digest.

object_bindings.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical sorting and uniqueness by (role,digest), then checks all evidence, pack, semantic, and qualification bindings.

dependency_digests.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical order/uniqueness by (kind,identifier) and exact mandatory PACK, SEMANTIC_PROFILE, and WORDING_POLICY joins.

qualification_denominators.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical order, unique IDs/digests, exact subject/profile joins, and invalidation dependencies.

qualification_evidence_bindings.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical receipt order and exact equality with the case's non-null qualification-receipt set.

observation_profiles.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical ordering and uniqueness by profile_id and canonical digest.

evidence_atoms.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical ordering and uniqueness by evidence_id.

derivations.$comment: The Python validator requires canonical ordering and uniqueness by derivation_id.

transitionCase.$comment: All cross-object identity, digest, semantic, temporal, applicability, replay-content, and invalidation joins are fail-closed in cisco_toolkit.transition_contract.validate_transition_case.
